By casting the creature before combat, the opponent sees it and can plan blocks accordingly. More importantly, Slickshot Show-Off could have been plotted here instead (paying 1R to exile it for a future free cast), preserving both Emberheart Challengers for a later turn where they could be deployed alongside the plotted Slickshot for a more explosive turn. However, since the opponent only has a Llanowar Elves as a blocker, casting Emberheart Challenger pre-combat to attack with haste is reasonable — the main issue is that it should ideally be cast before combat anyway since it has haste. The real sequencing concern is whether plotting Slickshot Show-Off would have been better use of the 2 mana this turn, saving Emberheart Challenger for turn 3 alongside the plotted Slickshot on turn 4. But playing the hasty 2/2 to pressure immediately is defensible. Actually, the creature has haste so it needs to be cast pre-combat to attack — that's fine. The question is whether plotting Slickshot would have been better. With Might of the Meek in hand, deploying Emberheart now and attacking (potentially using Might of the Meek to trigger prowess and valiant) is a strong aggressive line. This is reasonable.
